source: សៀវភៅស្ដីពីដំណាំដំឡូងមី (Book on Cassava), Part 2, UNDP-supported capacity-building programme for cassava, March 2015 (citing USDA nutrient data and Julie A. et al., 2009)
text:
The source presents detailed nutrient-composition tables for cassava root, citing USDA nutrient data. Per 100g of raw cassava root: approximately 160 kcal (about 8% of a Reference Daily Intake/RDA), 38.06g carbohydrate (about 25% RDA), 1.36g protein (about 2.5% RDA), 0.28g total fat (about 1% RDA), 0mg cholesterol, and 1.8g dietary fiber (about 5% RDA). Vitamin content includes folate (27 micrograms, about 7% RDA), niacin (B3), pyridoxine (B6), riboflavin (B2), thiamin (B1), vitamin A, vitamin C (about 20.6mg, roughly 34% RDA), vitamin E, and vitamin K. Mineral content includes sodium, potassium (271mg, about 6% RDA), calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, manganese, copper, and selenium, with calcium and iron each contributing only a small percentage of RDA.

A second table (citing Julie A. et al., 2009) compares nutrient ranges across cassava root, cassava leaves, and a broader 'cassava' category, and shows cassava leaves are markedly higher than the root in several nutrients: notably higher crude protein content (leaves in a range roughly an order of magnitude higher than the root's ~1.36g/100g), much higher vitamin A content (leaf ranges in the thousands of micrograms per 100g versus negligible amounts in the root), and higher ascorbic acid (vitamin C), calcium, and iron content than the root. This supports the source's broader point (echoed elsewhere in the document) that cassava leaves are a nutritionally valuable food source, not just a byproduct, particularly for vitamin A and protein.
caveat: The two source tables contain extensive row-by-row numeric detail (full vitamin and mineral profiles with exact ranges) that was not fully transcribed cell-by-cell here; only headline figures and the qualitative leaf-vs-root comparison are captured with confidence. A dedicated high-resolution re-read of these two tables would be needed if exact per-nutrient figures are required.
